title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World
slides: Why would Meta build an AI pet app?
Waddle World launches as a standalone product
But it's not a game or a social network
Pet apps could reshape Meta's AI engagement metrics
Ask one question: what data do virtual pets collect?
thread_text:
1. Meta bets on virtual pets

A new standalone app called Waddle World is reportedly in development. It is not a game and not a social network.

2. From feed to companion

Instead of scrolling, users would care for an AI pet. Meta wants daily habits that do not depend on friends posting.

3. Engagement without the feed

A pet needs attention every day. That gives Meta a reason to send notifications and open the app even when nothing social is happening.

4. New metrics, new questions

If pet apps work, time spent and daily returns could rise. But the model only works if the pet feels personal, which means data.

5. What does your pet know?

Open your phone settings and check what an AI companion app can access. Would you trade that data for a virtual pet?

Meta is reportedly building a standalone app where you care for an AI pet instead of scrolling a feed. 🐾

If it works, time spent and daily returns rise — but only if the pet feels personal, and that means your data. 🤔

For anyone creating content, this is another signal that platforms are chasing habits, not feeds.
